rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (kp 6.0, base 1.2) scored 123.3, below iteration 1's 160.6, and oval finishes fell to 0. max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.063 m on all tracks whatever the speed (1.0 or 1.2) and gain (5.0 or 6.0). Line-loss events stayed at about 1 per run. Steering authority and speed are therefore not the binding limit. The Evaluator's third branch applies: line loss persists at about 1 per run with max_error near 0.06 m, which points to the sensor edge. The outer sensors at x = ±0.04 m (footprint edge about ±0.046 m) lose the line before the robot is corrected, and the 0.06 m off-track limit is then reached. Change: widen the sensor array to ±0.06 m, using 7 sensors at 0.02 m spacing (x = -0.06, -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06). The 0.02 m spacing keeps the 25 mm tape covered between sensors, so the sum of readings does not drop to zero on the line. Weights are scaled antisymmetrically to [-1, -0.67, -0.33, 0, 0.33, 0.67, 1], so the signal scale and sign convention match iteration 1. Controller is reverted to iteration 1's best setting (base 1.2, kp 5.0, kd 0.8, ki 0.02, last_direction) so this race isolates the geometry change against the 160.6 baseline. Expected result: line_loss_events fall toward 0 and max_error drops below about 0.055 m, with more oval finishes. Hypotheses: (a) the line-loss event at the sensor edge is the cause of the off-track exit; (b) with a wider array, kp 5.0 will be enough to hold the line. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion time, rms and max error, line-loss events, steering oscillation, controller errors. If line loss is still about 1 per run with max_error near 0.06 m, the next step is to test whether the 0.04 m spacing or the sensor size (0.016 m) is limiting.
